Scope the release dry run's ref check to refs it can move (#290)

tools/release-dry-run.sh hashed the whole git for-each-ref listing
before its run and in step 6, so a ref that another worktree moved
during the run failed it, although the dry run had moved nothing (TODO
279, seen on the PR 284 gate). Step 6 now compares only the refs that
the dry run could itself move, read from the worktree that holds the
script before and after: the branch HEAD names, or that it is
detached; the commit HEAD resolves to; and every tag and note with its
object name. It prints both snapshots on a mismatch, so the failure
names the ref that differs. It then fails when a ref that git
for-each-ref lists from that worktree contains the dry-run commit,
read with replace refs, grafts and the shallow file turned off, so
none of them can hide such a ref. In a shallow clone, the leak check,
which reads with the shallow file turned off, finds the parents of a
commit at the shallow boundary missing, so there it can fail the run
on git's message about them or naming a ref that does not contain the
dry-run commit; release-dry-run.yml checks out the whole history, so
its run is not shallow. The tag and note listing of each snapshot and
the listing of the leak check fail the run when git writes anything
to standard error while it lists, as when git for-each-ref skips a ref
whose name it rejects, with a warning, and still exits 0. Neither
failure says who wrote the ref, since another worktree's write, or a
ref that held the dry-run commit before the run, fails the run too.
The script makes that commit with git commit-tree, which prints the
name of the commit it writes, saves that name for step 6, never
reading a later HEAD, and moves the throwaway worktree's HEAD to it
with git update-ref, which fails if that HEAD is no longer at the
parent it read. Every git call of the
script after the before snapshot other than the reads of step 6, the
exit cleanup's included, runs with hooks, the core.fsmonitor program
and a pager turned off, and every git process of the dry run with lazy
fetching turned off. After its first 3 git calls past the before
snapshot, which list the filter drivers, find the info/attributes file
and name the empty tree, every git process of the dry run, its tools'
included, reads no attribute file other than info/attributes and, in
git archive, the .gitattributes files of the tree it archives and, in
the git check-attr that reads the filter drivers of the dry-run
commit, those of that commit, and runs with every filter driver turned
off that the configuration read from the script's worktree defines or
that info/attributes names, and, from step 1 on, every one that an
attribute gives a path of the dry-run commit. A driver name with an
equals sign fails the run, as does a git that does not refuse a
GIT_ATTR_SOURCE that names no tree with exit 128 and its own message
for that refusal alone on standard error, which cmp compares byte for
byte.

So no filter runs during a git call of the dry run, whatever the
configuration that git reads in any worktree defines, other than a
driver that the info/attributes file, or the tree that git archive
archives, comes to name during the run.

No git call of the script asks for a textconv or diff driver, a
signature, an editor or automatic maintenance, and the snapshot and
leak-check reads read no index and no file content and write to no
terminal. So no other program that git can run from its configuration
or from attributes runs during a git call of the script.

The git calls of the tools that the script runs are covered only by
the lazy-fetch, attribute and filter settings.

The run fails closed unless the throwaway worktree's HEAD is at the
dry-run commit once moved there. The git commit-tree runs with commit
signing turned off, so the dry-run commit is never signed. A git error
in either check, in reading the filter drivers, or in making or
reading the dry-run commit or moving HEAD to it, fails the run with
exit 1 and is never read as an empty listing. The exit cleanup is set
before the GIT_ATTR_SOURCE check makes its temporary file, and runs on
every exit of the run, one that HUP, INT or TERM causes included. It
tries to remove that file and the throwaway worktree once the script
holds the name of each; a removal that fails leaves its entry behind,
and so does a signal that ends the run after mktemp has made the file
or the worktree's folder and before the script holds its name, or one
that no trap can catch, such as KILL. Before it goes on or fails, the
run clears the name of the temporary file of the check of
GIT_ATTR_SOURCE, so that the exit cleanup cannot remove a file that
another process makes later under that name, and then tries to remove
the file itself, and fails if that removal fails; a signal that ends
the run between that clearing and that removal, or a failure of that
removal, leaves the file behind, since the exit cleanup then has no
name to remove.

This narrows a release-integrity check on purpose and needs the
maintainer's acceptance. Step 6 newly catches a commit on a detached
HEAD, and a detach or an attach at the same commit, which the old hash
missed because git for-each-ref lists no HEAD. The script's header
states what step 6 no longer catches, and what it does not see, in
these words:

Residual: the proof does not catch the deletion of any ref outside
tags and notes other than the branch the script's worktree has checked
out, such as another branch, a remote-tracking ref, refs/stash or a
refs/replace/ ref; or a move or creation of such a ref at a commit
that does not contain the dry-run commit, at an annotated tag that
peels to such a commit, or at an object that peels to no commit, such
as a tree or a blob. It does not see the HEAD or
the per-worktree refs of any worktree other than the script's
worktree, the throwaway worktree included, or a ref outside refs/
other than HEAD, such as ORIG_HEAD, of any worktree, the script's
worktree included, so such a ref put on the dry-run commit does not
fail it. It does not see a write to a ref made after the after
snapshot, such as a tag that another worktree makes then, other than
a ref that the leak check, which follows that snapshot, finds to
contain the dry-run commit. It does not see anything the exit cleanup
does, or a ref moved and then restored between the 2 snapshots.

A ref that another worktree writes during the run fails the proof
only when it is a tag or a note, when it is the HEAD of the script's
worktree or the branch that worktree has checked out, when it is a ref
that git for-each-ref lists from the script's worktree, created or
moved onto the dry-run commit or a descendant of it, or when git fails
or writes to standard error while it lists the refs of a snapshot or
of the leak check, as it does for a ref whose name it rejects; any
other such write is outside the proof. TODO 279 does not record which
ref moved on the PR 284 gate, so whether this change would have
avoided that failure is unknown.

tools/test-release-dry-run-refs.py runs the whole script, copied byte
for byte into throwaway folders with stand-ins for the tools it calls,
so bash itself reads every line of it. Its 44 ref cases each build a
repository and make writes at up to 5 points: a git stand-in first on
PATH makes another worktree's writes before the dry run adds its
worktree, the move of that worktree once it is added in cases 42 and
44, its move after the dry run reads the parent of its commit in case
43, and, once the dry run's worktree is at the commit its git
commit-tree wrote, the dry run's own writes, or in cases 28 and 29
another worktree's; the stand-in of step 5 makes late writes after
that step. Every ref case but cases 31 and 43 must reach all 5 points;
case 31 must stop at the dry-run commit, before the fifth, and case 43
must stop when the move of that HEAD to it fails, before the fourth.
Each ref case checks that exactly the refs it names change, and that
the dry-run commit has the parent, identity, dates, message and tree
it must have. Its 12 cases on fail-closed reading make no ref writes:
11 require the run to end at the call or tool that fails, with no
later step, tool or git call other than the exit cleanup and the other
call of a pipeline, a mktemp, cmp or rm of the GIT_ATTR_SOURCE check
that fails among them, and 1, with no tag and no note, requires it to
pass. 1 more case runs the dry run in a caller locale other than C and
requires its check of GIT_ATTR_SOURCE to run with LC_ALL set to C,
its temporary file to be gone before the run goes on, and a file made
later under that file's name to be left in place, 1 more ends the
run with HUP, INT or TERM during that check and requires the run to
end by that signal and that file to be gone, 1 more ends it with TERM
once the script has removed that file and another file is made under
its name, and requires the run to end by TERM and that other file to
be left in place, 1 more writes a tag, and in turn a branch,
whose name git rejects, and requires the run to fail at the listing
that skips it, and 1 more leaves tags and notes refs on the dry-run
commit of an earlier run, or on a child of it, and requires the leak
check to name them. 1 more case turns commit signing on in the
configuration and requires the dry run to pass without signing, and 1
more writes 8
hooks to the configured hook folder and requires the dry run to pass
with none of them run. 7 more each configure programs that git runs
from its configuration or from attributes: a core.fsmonitor program,
clean and smudge filters, a process filter, pagers that pager.<command>
and core.pager name with the run on a terminal, textconv and diff
drivers, an editor and a sequence editor,
and the upload-pack program of a promisor remote; each
requires the dry run to run none of them, the last by failing closed
at its read of a missing blob. 1 more defines 3 filter drivers only
for linked worktrees, through a conditional include, and gives them
paths through info/attributes, a committed .gitattributes file and
core.attributesFile, with a packager stand-in that runs git archive;
the dry run must pass with none of them run. 1 more requires a driver
named a=b to fail the run before any of its commands runs. 1 more
reads git's trace2 log and requires every git call of the script
after the before snapshot other than one in the form of the reads of
the 2 snapshots or the leak check, wherever the script makes it, the
exit cleanup's included, to run with hooks and the core.fsmonitor
program turned off and to start no program other than git, every one
to run with lazy fetching turned off, and every one after the first 3
and the GIT_ATTR_SOURCE check also to run with the attribute settings
and both configured filter drivers turned off. Each of those 4 is
exempt from these settings only in the argument form and with the
GIT_ATTR_SOURCE that the script gives it, and only once, so a later
run in that form must run with them. 1 more, the text
case, requires 4 blocks, the residual and the 2 remainders that the
script's header states and the residual of the test that its
docstring states, each to be 1 whole paragraph, the same word for
word in every text that holds it, so a word added before a block's
first words or after its last words fails it too. It also requires 5
sentences that are repeated inside paragraphs that differ, the
listing rule, the scope of another worktree's writes, the
shallow-clone caveat, the exemption of the trace2 case and the
clearing of the name of the check's file, to be held once, word for
word, in each text that holds them. The docstring
repeats the residual; this message as .github/squash/290.txt commits
it, and the description and this message at the top of the export,
repeat all 4. CI has neither of the last 2, so there the case
compares the header's residual with the docstring's copy and each of
the 4 blocks with the committed message, and says that it skips the
other 2.

Residual of the test: stand-ins replace the packaging, the
gates and the site rewrite, which the next step of release-dry-run.yml
runs with the real tools, and the script runs with an environment that
the test fixes, with a git stand-in first on PATH in the ref cases and
a git wrapper there in some other cases, not with those of that
workflow. A change to the script is caught only when it changes
what a case observes, so a change that acts only outside the cases,
such as one that tests for the stand-ins or for the workflow's
environment, or that moves a ref no case writes or stops step 6
reading one, is not caught. The text case compares only the 4 repeated
blocks, each as 1 whole paragraph, and the 5 repeated sentences, each
as a run of words, so it does not catch a paragraph added next to a
block, words added next to a sentence, a change to any other paragraph
or sentence, a change to a copy in a text that it does not read, such
as a comment of the script below its header, or a change to a text
that the checkout lacks, as CI lacks PR-BODY.md and SQUASH-MSG.
The cases run on 1 git version with its default ref backend.

The test's first version of 21 cases, run against the unchanged
script, failed the concurrent cases and passed the detached commit;
against this change all 74 cases pass. Each of 14 mutants that remove
1 stated rule failed at least 1 case of the 33-case suite, each of 10
later mutants failed at least 1 case of the 36-case suite, each of 9
script mutants that the 36-case suite passed fails at least 1 case of
the 34-case suite and of the 35-case suite, and each of 13 script
mutants of the capture fix, 8 of which the 35-case suite passed, fails
at least 1 case of the 44-case suite. The 47-case suite fails cases
37 and 38 against the script before the graft and shallow fix, and
fails each of 6 script mutants that remove 1 rule of the leak check,
the signing rule of git commit or the HEAD in the message of case 31,
or that call git by its absolute path before the before snapshot. The
52-case suite fails the hook case against the script before the
plumbing fix, whose run passes there while a hook keeps the commit
that git commit made in a ref, and fails each of 11 mutants of the
plumbing fix. The 61-case suite fails 6 cases against the script
before the configured-program fix, the core.fsmonitor case among them,
whose run passes there while that program runs 6 times and makes the
parent of the dry-run commit, and fails each of 12 mutants of that
fix. The 66-case suite fails 6 tests against the script before the
attribute fix, the linked-worktree filter case among them, whose run
passes there while 3 filter drivers that only the configuration of a
linked worktree defines run 35 times, and fails each of 15 mutants of
that fix. The 67-case suite fails 2 tests against the script and the
texts before the refusal fix, the case on the filter settings, in
which that script reads 4 other outcomes of its first git check-attr
as git's refusal of a GIT_ATTR_SOURCE that names no tree, and the text
case, and fails each of 4 mutants of that fix. The 69-case suite
fails the case on the filter settings against the script before the
line-ending fix, which reads git's message followed by a blank line,
or without its newline, as git's refusal, and fails each of 6 script
mutants that the 67-case suite passes, or its fail-closed cases for
the 2 that change only a failure path, and each of 6 mutants of the
texts, each changing 1 word, that its text case passes. The suite of
the NUL fix, still of 69 cases, gives the first git check-attr 6 more
outcomes and fails the script before that fix, which reads git's
message with a NUL byte after it, before it, inside it or before its
newline as git's refusal, since a command substitution drops every NUL
byte; that fix compares standard error with cmp. It fails each of 5
mutants of that fix, and its text case, which now reads each block as
1 whole paragraph, fails each of 7 mutants of the texts that add words
before or after a block in its paragraph, which the text case before
it passes. The suite of the probe cleanup fix, of 72 cases, fails the
script before that fix in its signal case, whose run leaves the
temporary file of the GIT_ATTR_SOURCE check when HUP, INT or TERM ends
it, and fails each of 6 rule removals that the 69-case suite passes
and each of 4 mutants of that fix. The suite of the claims fix, still
of 72 cases, fails in its locale case a script that does not clear
the name of that file once it has removed it, and in both runs of its
pager case, the core.pager run included, a script without --no-pager.
The suite of the listing fix, of 74 cases, fails the script before
that fix in its skipped-ref case, whose run passes there with a tag or
a branch whose name git rejects, and in its new signal case, and fails
each of 3 mutants of that fix, 1 of which the trace2 case before it
passes. The suite of the text fix, still of 74 cases, fails each of 2
script mutants that ignore the signal of a signal case, whose run the
signal cases before that fix pass, and each of 5 mutants of the texts,
each changing 1 word of 1 repeated sentence. The release dry run
workflow and tools/run_all_checks.sh run it before the dry run, and
tools/test-run-all-checks.py records the new digest of
tools/run_all_checks.sh after a reading of the whole script. The
workflow header now counts 7 test suites.

tools/test-version-selectors.sh now reads the dry run's version
selector in the form that runs git with git_off, runs the script's own
settings before it, from its exports of TZ and GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH
through its check of GIT_ATTR_SOURCE, git_off and the attribute and
filter settings included, refuses an extracted block that is not a
run of whole lines of its source, and requires each of its 4
structural checks to run once for each of its 3 sites and for no
other site.
